slip.document:
# Shift Handoff and Progress Note - Medical-Surgical Unit
Juniper Memorial Hospital - 4 West

## Patient Demographics
- Patient: Rosa Osei
- MRN: 4920188
- Room: 412-B
- Attending: Brandon Banerjee, MD
- Primary Nurse: Megan Maddox, RN
- Date: 10/14/2026
- Shift: 0700-1930
- Diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated diverticulitis

## Reference Baseline and Allergies
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Known Allergies | Ciprofloxacin (severe hives, angioedema) |
| Baseline Weight | 164 lb |
| Baseline BP | 118/74 mmHg |
| Code Status | Full Code |

## Objective Findings (1500 Assessment)
- Vitals: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 99.1 °F.
- GI: Abdomen soft, moderately tender to palpation in right lower quadrant with guarding, active bowel sounds across all quadrants.
- Access: 20-gauge peripheral IV in right forearm, patent with 0.9% normal saline infusing at 75 mL/hr.
- Intake/Output: Total oral intake 450 mL clear liquids; urine output 620 mL clear amber via urinal/bedpan across shift.

## Interventions and Medications Administered
- Administered IV ciprofloxacin 400 mg over 60 minutes at 1400 without immediate complication.
- Administered IV acetaminophen 1,000 mg at 1200 for reported abdominal pain rated 5/10; pain decreased to 2/10 at 1300 reassessment.
- Held regular diet per order; tolerated ice chips and clear liquids without nausea or vomiting.

## Plan of Care for Night Shift
- Continue clear liquid diet as tolerated.
- Administer scheduled IV metronidazole 500 mg at 2200.
- Repeat CBC with differential drawn at 0400 on 10/15/2026.
- Notify Dr. Banerjee for temperature greater than 101.0 °F or acute worsening of abdominal pain.

edge.title: Machine Down, Production Line Stalled
edge.scenario: You are a commercial electrician troubleshooting a critical automated packaging line that suddenly tripped out on an industrial plant floor. Plant manager Greg arrives visibly stressed, holding a radio and demanding you bypass diagnostics with your testing tools to flip the main breaker back on immediately. Thousands of dollars are being lost every minute the conveyor belt stays idle.
edge.persona: Greg is the operations manager at the packaging facility, pacing beside the locked electrical cabinet while holding a blaring two-way radio. He is impatient, authoritative, and focused entirely on the lost revenue ticking by each minute.
edge.opening: Put the meters away and just reset the damn main breaker! We're burning ten grand every five minutes this line sits dead. Whatever tripped it probably cleared itself, so flip it back on right now—I'll take full responsibility!
edge.goal: De-escalate Greg's urgency and gain his consent to complete full multimeter and insulation testing before attempting any breaker reset.
criteria: Acknowledges the high financial stakes of the production stoppage before defending testing protocols.
Explains clearly in plain terms why testing with instruments prevents catasrophic equipment destruction or injury.
Refuses firmly to bypass safety diagnostics or energize blind.
Provides an honest, realistic estimate of the testing timeline and an immediate plan of action.
